pr.title: gvn: bail out unavoidable non-ssa locals in repeat
pr.author: dianqk

issues.title: GVN makes an incorrect index access

analysis.summary: GVN had to stop simplifying indexed projections of repeated arrays when the index is a non-SSA local and the resulting value cannot be converted to a local. Otherwise simplification could use a later-modified index, which the linked issue calls an incorrect index access and which can introduce an out-of-bounds access.
analysis.originalLogic: In `VnState::project`, when handling `ProjectionElem::Index(idx)` for a value known as `Value::Repeat`, the old code returned the repeated inner value directly (`return Some(*inner);`). It did not record whether `self.locals[idx]` was absent, i.e. whether the index was a non-SSA local. The surrounding place simplification could then continue even though resolving the place depended on a non-SSA index.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation treated a repeat-index projection as independent of the index and continued GVN simplification when the index local had no SSA value. In the reported shape, `array = [*val; 5]; elem = &array[idx1]; idx1 = idx2; RET = *elem;` this could allow the dereference `*elem` to be rewritten using the already modified `idx1`, which the PR describes as transforming `*elem` to `array[idx1]` even though `idx1` has been modified. The fix instead bails out when a non-SSA index was seen and the value cannot be resolved via `try_as_local`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR containing a repeated array/aggregate `Value::Repeat`, followed by an `Index` projection using a local that is non-SSA (`self.locals[idx].is_none()`), especially when that index local is subsequently overwritten before the projected reference is dereferenced. The supplied custom-MIR tests cover both a repeated place (`[*val; 5]`) and a repeated local (`[val; 5]`).
analysis.trigger: GVN processes an indexed projection of a `Value::Repeat` and observes a non-SSA index local. The bail-out path is reached when later simplification cannot turn the projected value into a local (`try_as_local` fails). Concrete shape: `array = [*val; 5]; elem = &array[idx1]; idx1 = idx2; RET = *elem;` with `idx1` non-SSA and modified after `elem` is created.
preconditions: GVN is enabled for the MIR body.
The index local is non-SSA, detected as `self.locals[idx].is_none()`.
The index local can be updated after the reference/place is formed, so a later use of that index is not equivalent to the original indexed access.
The projected value cannot be simplified to a local via `try_as_local`; only then does GVN return `None` and retain the original dereference.
pitfalls: Do not conflate the borrow of the array through `elem` with the bug: the unsafe condition is using a later-modified, non-SSA index, not merely that a borrow exists.
Do not blanket-disable all repeat-index simplification: the regression test keeps the local case optimized to `_0 = copy _3`, while the place case retains `_0 = copy (*_5)` / `_0 = copy (*[[ELEM]])`.
A retained test name or old comment does not prove which pass is wrong; compare the actual value assignments in the MIR before/after snapshots.
The fix is conservative: the PR says it could perhaps use `array[0]`, but prefers bailing out rather than constructing a more specific replacement.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a custom-MIR test under `tests/mir-opt/` with `//@ test-mir-pass: GVN` and `EMIT_MIR` snapshots. Include both `repeat_place` (`array = [*val; 5]`) and `repeat_local` (`array = [val; 5]`), with `idx1 = idx2` between taking `elem = &array[idx1]` and reading `RET = *elem`. Check that the place case retains the original dereference (`_0 = copy (*_5)`) rather than introducing an access using the updated index, and that the local case may simplify to the repeated local (`_0 = copy _3`). Add executable assertions such as `repeat_place(0, 5, &0) == 0` and `repeat_local(0, 5, 0) == 0`, described by the test as checking that no out-of-bounds access is introduced. Rely on MIR snapshots plus the test harness; no compiler execution was performed here.
